paragraphs: Haringey Council approves its own foster carers, and children in its care may also live with independent agencies such as those on this page. Since 1 October 2026 the council's fostering recruitment has been run through the North London Fostering Hub, which Camden leads on behalf of Barnet, Camden, Enfield, Hackney, Haringey and Islington, building on a partnership between the six boroughs that dates back to 2012. Enquiries now go through Foster North London.

The council says there are many children in Haringey who need foster carers, and you do not need to be a parent yourself to apply. It particularly welcomes men who want to foster and runs support groups for them.

The route has five steps: a first call with a social worker, a home visit, a compulsory three-day Skills to Foster course, an assessment with weekly home visits, checks and references that can take up to four months, and finally the fostering panel. Once approved you have a supervising social worker, an experienced carer as a mentor through your first placement, support around the clock all year and specialist training.
Haringey does not publish its allowances on the pages we read, so ask the hub and two or three of the agencies below for their figures, and compare the support each offers, before you decide.

sources.title: Camden chosen to lead new North London Fostering Hub (Camden Council)
